schedule_days_sample.task_description: Formulate a business problem, inspect target distributions, identify anomalies, and analyze feature correlations.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Fundamentals architectural concepts and implementation patterns for Machine Learning.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: Successful machine learning begins with understanding data distributions and domain constraints before writing a single model training call. In exploratory data analysis, you evaluate target class balance (imbalanced classes require metrics like Macro F1 rather than raw accuracy), calculate feature correlation matrices to identify multicollinearity, and inspect distributions for outliers or missingness. Establishing an objective baseline metric upfront provides a benchmark against which all future iterations are evaluated.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Perform complete exploratory data analysis on a public tabular dataset using Pandas. Plot histograms, calculate correlation heatmaps, and identify missing value distributions.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A reproducible EDA Jupyter notebook (`exploratory_data_analysis.ipynb`) with statistical distribution charts and data quality findings.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Confirm the notebook reports missing value counts, skewness metrics, and feature-target correlations.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Build automated feature transformation pipelines using Scikit-Learn ColumnTransformer.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Essential Concepts architectural concepts and implementation patterns for Machine Learning.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: Data leakage occurs when information from outside the training dataset (such as validation or test distributions) is used to create the model. Fitting a Scaler, Imputer, or TF-IDF vectorizer on the entire dataset before splitting leaks test distributions into training features, producing falsely optimistic validation scores that collapse in production. Best practice requires wrapping preprocessing and modeling inside a Scikit-Learn `Pipeline`, ensuring transforms fit strictly on training records.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Construct an automated ColumnTransformer pipeline handling numeric imputation/scaling, categorical encoding, and text TF-IDF vectorization on raw data.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A modular feature engineering script (`feature_pipeline.py`) exposing a clean transformer pipeline.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Fit the pipeline on training data, transform unseen validation data, and assert no data leakage warnings or dimension mismatches.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Train baseline linear models (Logistic Regression, Linear SVM) and non-linear tree models (Random Forest, LightGBM/XGBoost).
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Guided Exercises architectural concepts and implementation patterns for Machine Learning.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: Different algorithm families make contrasting architectural assumptions. Linear models (Logistic Regression, Linear SVM) assume decision boundaries are linear hyperplanes; they train rapidly, scale well to high-dimensional sparse text data, and provide interpretable feature weights. Tree-based ensembles (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) capture complex non-linear feature interactions and threshold splits automatically, without requiring strict feature scaling. Training both families establishes whether problem complexity justifies non-linear ensemble models.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Train at least three contrasting algorithms on your preprocessed data: Logistic Regression, Linear SVM, and a Gradient Boosted Tree. Track training time and convergence.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A model training script (`train_models.py`) saving trained model objects and initial evaluation logs.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Confirm that all models converge cleanly without convergence warnings and output class predictions.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Implement Stratified and Group-disjoint cross-validation, and evaluate precision, recall, and Macro F1.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Practical Mini-Project architectural concepts and implementation patterns for Machine Learning.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: Evaluating models on a single train-test split yields high variance estimates dependent on random partitioning. K-Fold cross-validation splits data into K subsets, iteratively training on K-1 folds and validating on the remaining fold. When records belong to distinct groups (such as multiple resumes from the same candidate or job postings from the same company), standard K-Fold causes data leakage. Group K-Fold ensures that all records from any given group reside exclusively in either the training fold or validation fold, providing true inductive generalization estimates.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Implement a 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation evaluation loop where the entire feature pipeline is fitted from scratch inside each training fold. Calculate Macro F1 and generate a confusion matrix.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A cross-validation script (`evaluate_cv.py`) printing per-fold Macro F1 scores, out-of-fold accuracy, and confusion matrix tables.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Verify that zero groups overlap between training and validation folds across all 5 splits.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Tune regularization penalties (L1/L2), tree depth, and learning rates using GridSearchCV.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Test Understanding architectural concepts and implementation patterns for Machine Learning.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: Unconstrained machine learning models tend to memorize noise in the training set (overfitting), resulting in poor generalization to new data. Regularization adds a mathematical penalty to the loss function to constrain model complexity. L2 regularization (Ridge) penalizes large weights by adding the sum of squared coefficients, shrinking weights smoothly. L1 regularization (Lasso) adds the sum of absolute values, driving non-informative feature weights to exactly zero (performing automatic feature selection). Hyperparameter tuning systematically sweeps parameter grids using inner cross-validation.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Configure a GridSearchCV pipeline tuning regularization strength `C` across 5 values. Plot validation Macro F1 versus training Macro F1 to identify the optimal complexity sweet spot.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A hyperparameter tuning experiment notebook (`hyperparameter_tuning.ipynb`) displaying validation curves and parameter rankings.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Confirm the selected best estimator exhibits balanced performance between training and cross-validation folds without catastrophic drop-off.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Understand containers, images, registries, and the difference between containers and virtual machines.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Fundamentals architectural concepts and implementation patterns for Docker.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: Containers virtualize at the operating system level, sharing the host Linux kernel while using kernel namespaces (PID, NET, MNT, IPC, UTS) to provide process isolation and cgroups to constrain resource usage (CPU, memory). Virtual machines virtualize hardware via a hypervisor, requiring an entire guest operating system per VM, which results in gigabytes of overhead and multi-minute boot times. Container images are read-only templates composed of layered filesystems, while containers are live, running instances of those images with a thin read-write layer on top. Public or private registries (like Docker Hub or GitHub Packages) store and distribute these images.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Install Docker Desktop or Docker Engine. Run `docker run --rm hello-world` to verify daemon connectivity, then run `docker run -it --rm alpine sh` to explore an isolated Linux container shell.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A terminal output log documenting successful execution of `docker version` and `docker info`.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Confirm Docker daemon is running and running containers appear in `docker ps`.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Practice Docker commands for running, inspecting, stopping, and cleaning up containers.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Essential Concepts architectural concepts and implementation patterns for Docker.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: Managing containers effectively requires proficiency with essential CLI commands. Running `docker run -d -p 8080:80 --name my-web nginx` pulls the Nginx image, starts it in detached mode, maps host port 8080 to container port 80, and gives it a friendly name. `docker ps` inspects running containers, while `docker logs -f my-web` streams application output. `docker exec -it my-web sh` opens an interactive shell inside a running container for live debugging. Finally, `docker stop`, `docker rm`, and `docker system prune` manage system resources and clean up dangling images.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Run a local Redis container in the background with a named volume. Connect to it via redis-cli inside the container, set a key-value pair, stop and restart the container, and verify data persists.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A shell script (`docker_commands_demo.sh`) demonstrating running, logging, executing inside, and cleaning up containers.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Execute the script and verify clean exit with no dangling containers left running.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Learn Dockerfile instructions, image layers, and build contexts.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Guided Exercises architectural concepts and implementation patterns for Docker.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: A Dockerfile is a declarative recipe for building a container image. Each instruction (FROM, COPY, RUN) creates an immutable filesystem layer that Docker caches. Instructions that change infrequently (such as installing system packages and dependencies) should be placed before instructions that change often (such as copying application source code); this maximizes cache reuse during iterative builds. Understanding `.dockerignore` prevents bloated build contexts by excluding `.git`, `__pycache__`, virtual environments, and sensitive `.env` files.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Write a `.dockerignore` file and author a Dockerfile for a Python application. Build the image with `docker build -t my-app:1.0 .` and verify that modifying a code file does not invalidate the `pip install` cached layer.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A valid `Dockerfile` and `.dockerignore` file with properly ordered layers for caching efficiency.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Run `docker build` twice; verify the second build prints `CACHED` on the dependency installation step.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Containerize a simple Flask or FastAPI application and verify local connectivity.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Practical Mini-Project architectural concepts and implementation patterns for Docker.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: Containerizing a web application involves configuring the service to listen on all interfaces (0.0.0.0 instead of 127.0.0.1, so external requests can reach the container), mapping ports correctly, and managing environment configuration. Passing environment variables via `docker run -e APP_ENV=production -e DATABASE_URL=...` decouples code from configuration. The containerized application should write logs directly to stdout/stderr so the Docker logging driver can capture and rotate them.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Create a minimal Flask app with two routes: `/` returning JSON status and `/health` returning HTTP 200. Containerize it, run the container with port mapping, and access both endpoints using curl or a web browser.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A complete containerized web service repository containing `app.py`, `requirements.txt`, `Dockerfile`, and `README.md`.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Run `curl http://localhost:5000/health` and verify HTTP 200 response with container logs showing request access.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Learn Docker Compose, networking, volumes, and environment configuration.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Test Understanding architectural concepts and implementation patterns for Docker.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: Modern web applications rarely run as a single container; they require web servers, databases, background workers, and caches. Docker Compose defines multi-container applications in a declarative `docker-compose.yml` file. Compose creates a private bridge network automatically, enabling containers to communicate using their service names as DNS hostnames (e.g., `postgresql://db:5432/mydb`). Named volumes ensure database data persists across container restarts, and `depends_on` defines startup order.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Write a `docker-compose.yml` linking your containerized Python web application to a PostgreSQL database container with a persistent named volume. Verify the web app connects to the database via hostname `db`.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A tested `docker-compose.yml` file launching a multi-service stack with persistent storage.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Execute `docker compose up -d`, insert data via the API, run `docker compose down`, restart with `docker compose up -d`, and verify data persists.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Study AWS Global Infrastructure (Regions, Availability Zones, Edge Locations) and the Shared Responsibility Model.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Fundamentals architectural concepts and implementation patterns for AWS.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: AWS organizes global infrastructure into geographic Regions (e.g. us-east-1, eu-west-1), each containing multiple physically isolated Availability Zones (AZs) connected by ultra-low-latency fiber. The Shared Responsibility Model defines security accountability: AWS is responsible for security 'OF' the cloud (physical facilities, host hardware, hypervisors, and managed service software patches), while the customer is responsible for security 'IN' the cloud (customer data encryption, IAM policies, OS configuration/patching, and network firewall rules).
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Diagram which security controls belong to AWS vs the customer across EC2, RDS, and S3.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A Shared Responsibility comparison matrix (`aws_shared_responsibility.md`) documenting security boundaries.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Confirm the matrix correctly attributes OS patching responsibility to customer for EC2 and to AWS for RDS.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Master IAM users, groups, roles, JSON policies, and the principle of least privilege.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Essential Concepts architectural concepts and implementation patterns for AWS.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: IAM is the security gatekeeper for all AWS API calls. Root accounts should never be used for daily tasks and must have MFA enabled. IAM Users represent individual humans; IAM Groups aggregate users sharing job functions; IAM Roles are assumed by AWS services (like EC2 or Lambda) to grant temporary security credentials via STS without embedding permanent secrets in code. IAM policies are JSON documents specifying Effect (Allow/Deny), Action (e.g. `s3:GetObject`), Resource (ARN), and Conditions following the principle of least privilege.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Author an IAM policy allowing read-only access to a specific S3 bucket while denying write access. Attach it to an IAM Role and verify permissions using the IAM Policy Simulator.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A validated JSON IAM policy file (`least_privilege_policy.json`) adhering to least-privilege principles.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Run the IAM Policy Simulator to verify that `s3:GetObject` evaluates to Allowed while `s3:PutObject` evaluates to Denied.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Design a custom VPC with public subnets, private subnets, Internet Gateway, and Security Groups.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Guided Exercises architectural concepts and implementation patterns for AWS.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: A VPC is an isolated virtual network dedicated to your AWS account. Designing a secure two-tier web application network requires creating: 1) Public subnets connected to an Internet Gateway via route tables, hosting public Application Load Balancers, and 2) Private subnets without direct internet ingress, hosting backend application servers and databases. Security Groups act as stateful virtual firewalls at the instance/ENI level, while Network ACLs (NACLs) provide stateless subnet-level packet filtering.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Design a VPC architecture diagram with CIDR blocks, route tables, and security group rules where database instances in private subnets accept traffic strictly from web instances.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A network architecture specification (`vpc_network_design.md`) detailing CIDRs, routing rules, and security group configurations.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Verify that database security groups allow inbound port 5432 exclusively from the web server security group ID (referencing SG IDs, not IP addresses).

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Launch an EC2 instance in a public subnet, host static assets in S3, and connect to a managed RDS database.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Practical Mini-Project architectural concepts and implementation patterns for AWS.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: Amazon EC2 provides resizable compute capacity with various instance families (general purpose, compute-optimized, memory-optimized). Amazon S3 provides highly durable (99.999999999% 11 9s) object storage for static files, media, and backups. Amazon RDS automates relational database administration (PostgreSQL, MySQL), providing automated snapshots, read replicas, and multi-AZ synchronous replication for instant automated failover during outages.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Deploy a containerized or Python application to an EC2 instance. Configure the application to store uploaded files in an S3 bucket and persist relational records to an RDS database.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: A deployment runbook (`cloud_application_deployment.md`) documenting instance launch, S3 bucket policy, and RDS database connectivity.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Confirm the application successfully persists data across both S3 and RDS endpoints without storing credentials in source code.

schedule_days_sample.task_description: Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and Auto Scaling Group (ASG) across multiple Availability Zones.
schedule_days_sample.learning_objective: Master Test Understanding architectural concepts and implementation patterns for AWS.
schedule_days_sample.explanation: High availability ensures applications survive hardware failure. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS), distributing incoming client traffic across multiple EC2 target instances in different Availability Zones based on health check responses. An Auto Scaling Group (ASG) dynamically adjusts the number of running EC2 instances based on CPU utilization or request count metrics, maintaining application availability and optimizing cost.
schedule_days_sample.exercise: Configure an ALB with a target group performing HTTP health checks on `/health`. Attach an Auto Scaling Group and simulate instance failure to observe automatic replacement.
schedule_days_sample.expected_output: An architecture document (`high_availability_architecture.md`) detailing multi-AZ redundancy and auto-scaling policies.
schedule_days_sample.verification_method: Terminate one EC2 instance manually and confirm the ALB continues serving traffic from the healthy instance while the ASG launches a replacement.
